events.text: An old herbalist with milky eyes stops you in the market and puts a thumb on your brow without asking. "Grey at the edges," she says. "You used it like a hammer. I have a little dew from the Moon-Well. It is not cheap."

effects.log: She tips your head back and lets one drop fall.

choices.text: Ask what else it would cost

effects.log: She looks at you a long while. "A season of carrying water up my mountain," she says. You carry it.
She shrugs. "It will not get better on its own," she calls after you.

events.text: A traveller at the inn tells the table about a spring in the north where the moon sits in the water all night, and the water heals eyes that have seen too much. Someone at the table has a flask of it, and is willing to part with it.

effects.log: The flask is cold even in your warm hand.

choices.text: Go north yourself and find the spring

effects.log: It is a hard road and a cold one, and the spring is exactly as they said.
It is only a story, probably. Your eye aches all the way home.

events.text: A blind monk taps his way into your courtyard and sits down as if invited. "You have a gift and you burned it," he says. "I burned mine too, once. Let me show you how the Moon-Well water is drawn."

effects.log: It takes all winter and most of your patience. In spring there is dew in the bowl.

choices.text: Offer the monastery a gift for his trouble

effects.log: He takes the gift for the monastery and gives you the bowl.
He goes, smiling, as if he expected nothing else.

events.text: For years the place where your root was has been a cold hollow. Then a hermit tells you there is a cave in the high ice where a body can be broken and grown again from nothing, if it survives the breaking.

effects.log: You climb.
You will go when you are stronger.

choices.text: You have made your peace with the hollow

effects.log: You thank the hermit and do not go. Some things are allowed to stay lost.

events.text: You wake in the night with a pain where your root was torn out, a new pain, like a bone trying to set. A healer you trust says it plainly: "It wants to grow back. It will kill you trying, or it will not."

effects.log: You lie down for the long fever, and let it try.

choices.text: Ask the healer to quiet it for now

effects.log: The healer quiets it. It is only sleeping.

choices.text: Ask the healer to quiet it for good

effects.log: The healer does, and the pain goes, and the hope with it.

events.text: An old fighter who lost his own root once, long ago, finds you. "Mine grew back," he says. "Harder than before. There is a way through the cold falls and the fire, and most who take it come out."

effects.log: He walks you to the falls and leaves you there.

choices.text: Ask him to come back in a few years

effects.log: He nods. "I will be here," he says. "Or I will not."

choices.text: Tell him you are done with roots

effects.log: He looks at you a long time and lets it be.

events.text: A young grey wolf has been following you at a distance for three days, never close, never gone. Tonight it sits on the far side of your fire and watches.

choices.text: Try to tame it: slowly, with your qi held low

effects.log: You sit down where you are, and wait, and hold out your hand.
You go around. It watches you go.

events.text: The leader of the grey wolves is down in the snow, panting, and the rest of the pack has gone quiet in the trees to see what you will do.

choices.text: End it, and take what it leaves

effects.log: You end it quickly and cleanly, as a hunter should.
You put your hand on it, and push your qi into it, and do not let go.
You lower your weapon.
